commits.subject: Give Soaked a source path git can actually resolve
commits.lede: `source` in the registry is passed straight to `git log -- <path>` by `npm run stamp`, so "src/royale (mode: water)" matched no path, produced no commits, and left Soaked as the one world on the grid with no "updated" date — and a failing freshness test on main.

commits.subject: Wallet: real balances in dollars, the spinning arc, and a test drop
commits.lede: Three things, and the first one was a real bug.

commits.subject: Water is the default now
commits.lede: /drop-zero opens SOAKED. It is the same 22 systems with ctx.mode flipped, and the water fight is the one worth playing — soakers, balloons, the glue gun, and last one dry wins. ?mode=classic is the way back to the bullets-and-health build for anyone who wants it, and /soaked stays a direct route.

commits.subject: SOAKED: the water-gun battle royale, wired up and playable
commits.lede: Eight systems behind ctx.mode === 'water', so one engine runs both games and classic stays byte-identical.

commits.subject: Wallet: hold more than one, and show what is actually in them
commits.lede: /wallet was a single card that said "payout address set" and then refused to say anything else. One address, no balances, no way to add a second — so somebody holding a MetaMask they have used for years AND a Base Account they made here last week could keep exactly one of them, and the app's only vocabulary for the other was "Create a Vibe Wallet". An invitation to make a third. The more wallets you had, the more ins

commits.subject: Arcade: a character shop with six originals you can buy and wear
commits.lede: The arcade had the loop that matters — pay, play, get paid — and one thing to spend on that you keep: hats. A hat is a good sink and a bad reason. Nobody opens a game to look at their hat; what people open a game to look at is who they are in it.

commits.subject: 📰 The front door opens with the paper instead of two buttons nobody pressed
commits.lede: "Start at the Terminal" and "The 3D hub" led `/game` — occupying the most valuable row on the page, pointing at two surfaces nobody uses. Both routes still exist and are still in the world list; they just no longer get the opening line.

commits.subject: 📜 Tap the date to see what changed — and fix the typecheck that was checking nothing
commits.lede: **First, the crash.** The wallet link I added to the Vibecoin chip referenced a `payout` variable I never declared. Tapping the chip white-screened the app with "payout is not defined". Fixed, and it reads the linked address when the panel opens rather than at mount, so linking a wallet and coming straight back shows the new state.

commits.subject: 🏝️ One plaza on Vibe Island, and a wallet you can actually find
commits.lede: **The layout.** Everything that costs or gives Vibecoin was scattered across a 110-unit island, and the character portal — one of the four things people actually use — sat at x = −34, sixty units and a jetpack ride from the shop it dresses you for. They now sit in one arc in the south-east:

commits.subject: 📬 The sign-in code autofills, and the box submits itself
commits.lede: Three things, and the first is the one that was actually asked for.

commits.subject: 🔐 The Vibe Wallet: a Base Account made with a passkey, and any wallet you own
commits.lede: Two doors now, for the two kinds of person who will open this card.

commits.subject: 🕰️ Re-stamp the worlds from a history deep enough to be true
commits.lede: `npm run stamp` reads each world's `source` out of the git log, and this repo is usually cloned shallow. The script guards the case where a path resolves to *nothing* — but not the case where it resolves to the clone's boundary commit, which is worse, because it looks like an answer. Twelve worlds were carrying 2026-07-21 for no reason other than that being as far back as the clone went.

commits.subject: 🏁 One Vibe Kart, and a lobby that starts the race for you
commits.lede: Two complaints, one shape. There were two Vibe Kart cards in the hub — `/kart` and `/kart-mp` — so the first decision a visitor made was one they could not yet have an opinion about, between two routes that render the same racetrack. And the multiplayer behind the second card was not really a lobby: it had a room code, a roster and a "Start race" button anybody could press, which works only if everyone is already sta

commits.subject: ✊ A table on the island: one hand against the house, provably fair
commits.lede: Walk up to the half-round table on the Vibe Island plaza, ante 25 ✦, and play one hand of rock-paper-scissors against the house. Smallest possible complete bet — no lobby, no opponent to find, ten seconds start to finish.

commits.subject: 🧭 Vibe Island leads, the running order moves to the top, and the map is current
commits.lede: **Ordering.** `ORDER` in `registry.ts` is the knob people reach for most, and it was seven hundred lines down, underneath every world entry. It is now the first thing in the file, with a comment saying that is what it is for. Vibe Island opens the collection — the gentlest door, works on a phone, the one to put in front of somebody who has never been here. Strange New Worlds moves to tenth. Orbit, the arcade and the

commits.subject: 🕰️ Every portal says when it last moved, and the wink finally gets used
commits.lede: Four of Jack's notes, and one thing found on the way.

commits.subject: 🛰️ ORBIT, invite links and a pot: the vibeverse gets something to bet on
commits.lede: The currency had places to spend it and no reason to want it. This is the reason: one shared sky, ten friends, one pot.

commits.subject: Air you can see through, and water on the worlds that have some
commits.lede: Two more of the things that separate a rendered frame from a diorama, and both turned out to be less about shading than about geometry.

commits.subject: One engine, two games: add the mode seam
commits.lede: ctx.mode is 'classic' (Drop Zero — bullets, health, a purple storm) or 'water' (SOAKED — soakers, dryness, the Downpour). One island, one set of 22 systems, and the difference is a lookup into mode/water.ts rather than a fork. Two battle royales would mean every bug fixed twice and every art pass done twice, and this project has already demonstrated how expensive one pass is.

commits.subject: The Odyssey gets a hull, and the planets get an atmosphere
commits.lede: The ship was a silhouette with blue stripes painted on it, which is fine at ninety units and is what you are looking at from nine. She now carries the `metal` bake at a 0.16-unit tile, sixty instanced greebles across the engineering hull, a lathed saucer at 96 segments, a deflector housing, a lit shuttlebay, seventy-six windows on two decks, a dorsal strobe, and running lights — port red, starboard green, the same co

commits.subject: People you can stand in front of, and columns that are not clip art
commits.lede: The characters were the weakest thing in the world and they were weak in the one place it costs most: three metres, face to face, which is where every conversation in this game happens. You walked up to a Vulcan master to ask her about Kolinahr and you were looking at a bowling pin.

commits.subject: A real renderer: HDR post, baked PBR surfacing, sky-probe IBL, ground scatter
commits.lede: The world shipped looking like coloured shapes on a coloured plane. Four things were missing and they turned out to be four specific things rather than a general lack of polish.

commits.subject: 🛍️ Vibecoin buys something you keep: cosmetics move onto the ledger
commits.lede: The arcade proved coins could be spent. It could not prove they were worth having, because everything you won there went straight back into the same machines — the currency had one sink and it was a loop.

commits.subject: 🖖 Strange New Worlds — twelve real Star Trek systems, and everyone on them talks back
commits.lede: /trek is the half of Star Trek where you shoot. This is the other half: make orbit somewhere nobody has been, run the sensors, then go down and ask it a question. No combat anywhere in it, on purpose.

commits.subject: Storm damage works; the beat was reading the wrong bar
commits.lede: Instrumenting dz:hit outside the zone showed a tick landing every simulated second, correctly sized — {amount: 0.504, shield: true} — with shield walking 100 -> 97.98 while health sat at exactly 100. skipToLive grants a full shield and applyDamage spends it first, like every other damage source, so the beat was watching a number that would not have moved for 200 seconds.

commits.subject: Floors and ramps were unbuildable on every street in every town
commits.lede: volumeClear() and isAnchored() contradicted each other about the ground. A wall's collider starts exactly on the lattice plane, but a floor's whole 0.25 m slab sits below it — the walking surface is the plane — and a ramp's staircase underhangs by half the wall thickness. Every POI has a solid apron whose top face IS that grid plane, so the very box isAnchored found as support was counted by volumeClear as an obstruc

commits.subject: Bot nameplates never compiled: one include, declared twice
commits.lede: three r160 prepends <colorspace_pars_fragment> to every non-raw ShaderMaterial, so PLATE_FRAG including it again declared LinearSRGBToLinearDisplayP3 twice and the whole fragment shader failed to compile — the nameplates over every bot rendered as nothing at all. This is the 'function already has a body' error the playtest surfaced during the harvest beat.

commits.subject: ⚡ GOD MODE — summon rain, snow and thunderstorms over the whole world
commits.lede: A chip next to the day/night switch opens a little palette: Clear, Rain, Snow, Storm. The day/night toggle is lobby-wide because everyone shares one sky; the weather is yours, because being the only person standing in a thunderstorm is funnier.

commits.subject: Loot: a held E can no longer be swallowed by the target it is waiting for
commits.lede: The interact edge was global: `prevInteract` latched true on every frame where nothing was in reach, so a press that began before the pickup arrived could never take it. Holding E while running onto a rifle — or while the gun you just knocked out of a chest settles — was silently refused until you let go and pressed again. The edge is now per-target (`takeArmed`), which is what the old rising edge was really trying t

commits.subject: dz-play: aim the build beats at ground the game will accept
commits.lede: build-place was never a builder bug. `aimPoint` puts the ghost at the full 10.5 m range when the look ray hits nothing, so clicking with the camera level in the middle of a POI asked for a wall inside somebody's concrete, `validate()` answered "blocked", and four correct refusals read as "nothing ever gets built". Instrumenting `collision.overlapBox` found the refusing box was a real slab genuinely intersecting the c

commits.subject: 🌆 Vibe City from the air: shadows, massing, rooftops, and a lighting grid
commits.lede: Pinch the camera out over Vibe City and what you saw was ninety extruded boxes standing on a painted plate. Nothing cast a shadow, so the towers appeared to hover a little above their own ground. Every roof was one flat colour — and roofs are most of what an aerial frame *is*, so the surface everybody looks at was the least-drawn thing in the scene. commits.subject: Loot: let a held interact sweep a pile, and name the containers
commits.lede: A floor item is a tap, but holding the key must still sweep a spill — walking into a chest's scatter with E down is how people actually collect loot. A quarter-second repeat in nearest-first order keeps that a sweep rather than a vacuum, so you can see what you took and let go before the fifth thing fills your last slot.

commits.subject: SOAKED foundations: multiplayer, the water rules, and a teammate who talks
commits.lede: Three pieces, none of which touch the single-player game that is already live.

commits.subject: Eleven levels, one per corner of the vibeverse
commits.lede: Ten new levels, and the interesting part is that they are different games rather than different paint.
